'''''Clinopodium vulgare''''', or the '''wild basil''' (not to be confused with the basils of the genus ''[[Ocimum]]''), is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Lamiaceae]].

==Description==
Wild basil is a perennial [[rhizomatous]] herb with square, upright, hairy stems and opposite pairs of leaves. The leaves are hairy, [[ovate (leaf)|ovate]] or [[lanceolate]] in shape, and have short or no stalks, wedge-shaped bases and bluntly-toothed margins. The [[inflorescence]] is a terminal [[spike (botany)|spike]] consisting of several loose whorls of clusters of flowers growing in the [[axil]]s of the leaves. Each flower has a short stalk, five sepals about {{cvt|10|mm}} long and five petals {{cvt|12|to|15|mm}} in length which are fused into a tube. The flowers are pink, violet or purple and have two lips. Each has four stamens, a long style and fused [[carpel]]s.<ref>{{Go Botany |genus=Clinopodium |species=vulgare |common=wild basil |access-date=2015-01-09}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Wild basil occurs in suitable locations in most of Europe, western and central Asia, North America and North Africa. Its typical habitat is dry [[grassland]] and [[heathland]], usually on limestone or chalky soils.<ref name=PFAF/> Though its distribution is patchy it is widespread and not threatened in the UK.<ref>[https://www.naturespot.org.uk/species/wild-basil Nature Spot - Wild Basil]</ref>

==Uses==
The leaves of wild basil are used as an aromatic herb in the preparation of food dishes and to make a herbal tea. They can also be used in the preparation of both a brown and a yellow dye.<ref name=PFAF>{{cite web |url=http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Clinopodium+vulgare |title=''Clinopodium vulgare'' |work=Plants For A Future |access-date=2015-01-09}}</ref>

This plant has traditionally been used as an [[astringent]], a [[cardiac stimulant]], an [[expectorant]], to [[Carminative|reduce flatulence]] and to [[Diaphoresis|increase perspiration]].<ref name=PFAF/> It has been used traditionally in Bulgaria for the healing of wounds and has been shown to have anti-bacterial properties.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Opalchenova, G. |author2=Obreshkova, D. |year=1999 |title=Antibacterial action of extracts of ''Clinopodium vulgare'' L. curative plant |journal=Drug Development and Industrial Pharmacy |volume=25 |issue=3 |pages=323–328 |pmid=10071825 |doi=10.1081/DDC-100102177}}</ref>

==Ecology==
Pollination is by [[bees]] and [[Lepidoptera]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wild Basil, Clinopodium vulgare - Flowers |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/wild-basil |website=Naturegate |access-date=2019-07-10}}</ref>
